seoTitle: How to Cite in Google Docs (2026 Citations Guide)
metaDescription: Use the built-in Citations tool in Google Docs to add sources in APA, MLA, or Chicago style and auto-generate a formatted Works Cited page.
intro: Google Docs has a built-in citation manager that removes the need for a separate bibliography generator. This guide covers opening the Citations sidebar, choosing your required style guide, adding source details, and generating a properly formatted Works Cited or References page automatically as you write.

steps.heading: Open the Citations sidebar
steps.body: Go to the Tools menu and select Citations to launch the built-in sidebar panel.

steps.heading: Select your citation style
steps.body: Choose your required style guide from the dropdown, including APA 7th edition, MLA 9th edition, or Chicago manual of style.

steps.heading: Add a new source
steps.body: Open the source wizard and choose the medium type, such as book, website, journal article, or online video.

steps.heading: Fill in source details
steps.body: Enter author names, publication years, titles, and publisher information into the corresponding data fields.

steps.heading: Insert in-text citations
steps.body: Place your cursor where a citation belongs in your paragraph and insert the parenthetical reference with a single click.

steps.heading: Generate your Works Cited page
steps.body: Use the automated bibliography builder to append a complete References or Works Cited page with proper hanging indents.

faq.question: Which citation styles does Google Docs support?
faq.answer: The built-in Citations tool supports APA, MLA, and Chicago style, covering the most common academic and professional formats.

faq.question: Does the bibliography update automatically as I add more sources?
faq.answer: Yes, the built-in bibliography engine regenerates your Works Cited or References page as you add or edit sources.

faq.question: Can I cite a website using the Citations tool?
faq.answer: Yes, the source wizard includes website URLs as a medium type alongside books, journal articles, and videos.

faq.question: Do I still need to alphabetize my sources manually?
faq.answer: No, the automated bibliography builder handles alphabetical sorting and proper hanging indents for you.
